html:
TotalSegmentator (University Hospital Basel): nnU-Net v2 networks that label 117 anatomical structures (organs, bones, muscles, vessels) in CT volumes, at 1.5 mm (five networks) or 3 mm (one, faster). Commercially usable (Apache-2.0 code and weights).

Commercial use: yes.

Measured

A small subset of real CT cases of the TotalSegmentator dataset (not the full test split), each run at its card's spacing (1.5 or 3 mm) in the same pipeline; mean over the cases of the Dice (0 to 1) averaged over the classes present, against the ground-truth segmentations (vertebrae_L6 of the subset has no counterpart and is skipped). Original = TotalSegmentator 2.18.0, default fp16 autocast. A paired check on one labeled CT at the variant's spacing. The compiled or TensorRT patch network runs inside the same PyTorch sliding-window pipeline. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

Limitations

  • On CUDA, stream=True keeps weights in CPU RAM and transfers each part once per volume. The five-part total model holds one part on the GPU at a time. All folds within the active part share the GPU.
  • On an RTX 5060 Ti with a 96 × 128 × 128 CT, total peak allocated memory was 1,140 / 876 MiB for resident / streamed portable and 1,013 / 748 MiB for kernels. Streaming preserved every predicted label in both modes.
